title: Customer data from India's Bank of Baroda leaked online, source and researcher say

Mon, July 27, 2026 at 6:20 AM EDT 1 min read

By Gopika Gopakumar and Ashwin Manikandan

MUMBAI, July 27 (Reuters) - Customer data from India's state-run Bank of Baroda, along with ‌internal documents, has been leaked on the dark web, ‌according to a source familiar with the matter and a cybersecurity researcher.

The lender ​said in a statement on Monday that it had started a forensic investigation and was working with relevant authorities after initial containment measures were implemented.

The breach involved a compromised employee email account, which resulted ‌in "unauthorised access to certain ⁠data", the Mumbai-based bank said.

"The bank's core banking systems were not accessed and continue to remain secure," ⁠it added.

The leaked data includes customer details, identification documents, loan papers and internal audit records, said cybersecurity researcher Srikanth L, founder of ​Cashless Consumer.

It ​was not immediately clear how ​many customers were affected.

The Reserve ‌Bank of India and India's cybersecurity regulator CERT-In did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The leak comes amid growing concerns over cybersecurity risks facing large companies and financial institutions that store vast amounts of customer and business data.

The data appeared on a ‌dark web site on Saturday night ​and was advertised as a cache containing ​more than 700 gigabytes ​of information, based on metadata analysis of the ‌site, Srikanth said.

In June, a cyberattack ​on Apple supplier ​Tata Electronics led to component design and specification documents linked to Apple and Tesla being leaked on the dark web.

Earlier this ​month, ransomware group ‌World Leaks posted files on the dark web related ​to India's largest nuclear plant.

(Reporting by Gopika Gopakumar and ​Ashwin Manikandan. Editing by Mark Potter)

content_html_zh:
戈皮卡·戈帕库玛和阿什温·马尼坎丹

2026 年 7 月 27 日星期一，美国东部时间上午 6:20 阅读 1 分钟

作者：戈皮卡·戈帕库玛和阿什温·马尼坎丹

孟买，7 月 27 日（路透社）——据知情人士和网络安全研究人员透露，印度国营巴罗达银行的客户数据以及内部文件已在暗网上泄露。

该银行在周一的一份声明中表示，在实施初步遏制措施后，它已开始进行法证调查，并正在与有关当局合作。

这家总部位于孟买的银行表示，此次泄露涉及员工电子邮件帐户被盗，导致“未经授权访问某些数据”。

“该银行的核心银行系统没有被访问，并继续保持安全，”它补充道。

Cashless Consumer 创始人、网络安全研究员 Srikanth L 表示，泄露的数据包括客户详细信息、身份证明文件、贷款文件和内部审计记录。

目前尚不清楚有多少客户受到影响。

印度储备银行和印度网络安全监管机构 CERT-In 没有立即回应置评请求。

这次泄密事件发生之际，人们越来越担心存储大量客户和业务数据的大公司和金融机构面临的网络安全风险。

斯里坎斯说，这些数据于周六晚上出现在一个暗网网站上，并被宣传为包含超过 700 GB 信息的缓存，根据该网站的元数据分析。

6 月，针对苹果供应商塔塔电子的网络攻击导致与苹果和特斯拉相关的组件设计和规格文件在暗网上泄露。

本月早些时候，勒索软件组织 World Leaks 在暗网上发布了与印度最大核电站相关的文件。

（戈皮卡·戈帕库玛和阿什温·马尼坎丹报道。 马克·波特编辑）
